summary: The patch changes SSTable.delete(Descriptor, Set<Component>) on cassandra-4.0 so it reads each component's lastModified once, sorts the components oldest first, and deletes them in that order. The goal is that a partial delete never changes the newest timestamp that LogFile.verifyRecord checks for REMOVE records. That is the right idea and follows the existing LogFile.deleteRecordFiles. On 4.0, though, the change misses the path the ticket describes and adds a regression. (1) LogTransaction.SSTableTidier.run still deletes the DATA file on its own before it calls SSTable.delete, so the 'DATA first, regardless of timestamp' order from ticket step 3 is still there. (2) The patch replaces FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm with FileUtils.delete, which ignores the File.delete() result. A failed delete is now silent: the tidier no longer queues a retry, it releases the transaction log anyway, and component files can be left behind. The ticket's test plan (additions to LogTransactionTest) is not done, there is no CHANGES.txt entry, and the commit message does not use the project format. The tool's requirement checks already flagged those last three, so I mention them only as context. The 4.0 base fits a bug-fix backport, and the patch adds no feature, config or protocol surface.

findings.rule: Error handling: no swallowed failures (cassandra-standards: error handling)
findings.problem: The old code called FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm, which throws FSWriteError when a delete fails. The new code calls FileUtils.delete(String), which returns File.delete()'s boolean, and that result is ignored. The only caller, LogTransaction.SSTableTidier.run (LogTransaction.java:401), depends on an exception: its catch adds the tidier to failedDeletions for a retry after GC and on restart. With this change a failed delete (EACCES, EIO, read-only filesystem) is silent. The tidier goes on to release parentRef, which lets the transaction log be removed while sstable components are still on disk. That leaks files with no log record left to clean them up on restart, and it skips any JVMStabilityInspector or disk-failure-policy handling the FSWriteError used to reach. The old code also used non-confirming FileUtils.delete for SUMMARY, presumably because SUMMARY may be missing; the patch now uses it for every component.
findings.fix: Keep the new sort, but delete each component with FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm. That matches LogFile.deleteRecordFiles, which deletes through LogTransaction::delete (Files.delete, logging only NoSuchFileException). If an absent SUMMARY really must be tolerated, check for that one case explicitly instead of downgrading every delete.

findings.rule: Ticket contract: SSTableTidier must not delete files out of timestamp order (CASSANDRA-21649 step 3)
findings.problem: In the ticket's scenario, SSTableTidier deletes files out of timestamp order after a compaction. On 4.0, SSTableTidier.run deletes the DATA file itself (`if (datafile.exists()) delete(datafile);`) before it calls SSTable.delete. The patch leaves this in place, so DATA is still always deleted first. If DATA is the newest non-STATS component, a crash right after that delete still changes the max timestamp and fails verifyRecord on restart. The patch fixes the order of the remaining components but not the DATA-first delete. I could not compare against the trunk patch Caleb Rackliffe reviewed, so I can't tell whether trunk changed this call site too.
findings.fix: Remove the separate DATA delete from SSTableTidier.run and let the sorted SSTable.delete handle every component. Keep the 'retry if DATA could not be deleted' behaviour by letting the exception from cs-1 propagate. If DATA-first was intentional (it makes a half-deleted sstable impossible to load), say so on the ticket and explain why the timestamp invariant still holds.

findings.rule: Ticket test plan: 'additions to LogTransactionTest'; a bug fix needs a regression test
findings.problem: The ticket's own test plan calls for additions to LogTransactionTest, but the 4.0 patch changes only SSTable.java. No test shows that a partial SSTableTidier deletion with staggered component mtimes now passes LogFile.verifyRecord, or that it failed before the fix. The requirement checks already flagged the missing tests; I list it here because it is a stated ticket deliverable.
findings.fix: Add a LogTransactionTest case that does the following. Create sstable components with increasing mtimes and make the DATA (or another non-STATS) component the newest. Log a REMOVE record. Simulate a crash partway through the tidier's deletes. Then assert that LogTransaction.removeUnfinishedLeftovers / verify succeeds.

findings.rule: Code style: comments say why, not what
findings.problem: The new comment refers to 'the overall SSTable timestamp' without saying which one. The invariant the code protects is the REMOVE record's updateTime that LogFile.verifyRecord checks (the max lastModified of the non-STATS components, see LogRecord.make). Without that link, a later change could reorder the deletes again, which is how this bug came about. The patch also drops the old 'DATA first' rationale and gives no reason why it is safe to give up.
findings.fix: Change the comment to something like: 'Delete in ascending lastModified order so that a partial delete leaves the max update time unchanged; LogFile.verifyRecord relies on this for REMOVE records (CASSANDRA-21649).'

findings.rule: Commit hygiene: CHANGES.txt entry and 'patch by ... ; reviewed by ... for CASSANDRA-N' commit message
findings.problem: The patch is a user-visible bug fix (startup failure after a crash) with no CHANGES.txt line under 4.0.22. The commit message 'Delete SSTables in last-modified order ...' does not use the project format, and the ticket has no Fix Version. The requirement checks already reported these; I include them only so the committer handles them together.
findings.fix: Add ' * Ensure SSTable files are deleted in order of last-updated timestamp (CASSANDRA-21649)' at the top of the 4.0.22 section, set the ticket's Fix Version for each target branch, and rewrite the commit message in the 'patch by X; reviewed by Y for CASSANDRA-21649' form.
